jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst - Payment Operations
jobs.description:
Company Description

Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.

Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.

Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.

As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.

For everyone, everywhere.

Job Description

More about our mission
and what we offer
.

THE ROLE

We are looking for a Senior Payment Operations Analyst who is passionate about our mission of Money Without Borders. You will partner with our Payment Operations organisation to help drive data-driven decisions that would improve the quality of our payment systems, making them smoother and more efficient.

The Payment Operations organisation is responsible for ensuring that our customers’ payments flow smoothly. The organisation focuses on resolving issues surrounding the movement of funds, to deliver a fast and convenient payment experience for our customers.

As a Senior Payment Operations Analyst, you will be driving our analytics effort to strengthen our quality assurance and control processes. You will identify how we can evaluate if payment processing flows are done right, and if not, what went wrong with them. You will own an attribution model to quality lapses, and work with other teams to improve the quality of payment processing. You will also be incorporating AI in your work, using AI to improve the quality review process.

This is a great opportunity for an analyst that has strong product thinking and is passionate about creating convincing analyses. It also allows you to work alongside the current developments in AI. You will also be part of a wider team of 150+ analysts that you can collaborate with on cross-team projects, have knowledge sharing sessions and bring ideas on how we can improve analytics across Wise.

This is an IC2 role. For more information on our Analytics Career Map and levelling structure, click here.

Please note that Wise does not provide visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

What You’ll Be Doing

Collaborate with various senior stakeholders in the organisation and effectively communicate your insights into real change for our customers. Join us in working towards our mission.

jobs.title: Middle Data Analyst
jobs.description:
What project we have for you

We’re looking for a Mid Data & Analytics Analyst to support analytics initiatives , primarily using first-party consumer and CRM data.
The role will combine hands-on data analysis with assessment of data availability, quality and system performance. The analyst will work alongside more senior analytics specialists, taking ownership of defined analytical tasks, supporting larger projects, and refreshing or extending existing analyses.
This is not a pure BI or dashboarding role. Visualization and data storytelling are important complementary skills, but the main focus is on understanding data, identifying issues and producing reliable analytical outputs.

What you will do

Prepare, clean and analyse first-party datasets using SQL and Python.
Perform exploratory and behavioral analysis across consumer, CRM and lifecycle data.
Assess the presence, completeness, consistency and usability of data across systems.
Analyse data flows and system performance, including topics such as data quality, freshness, latency and delivery.
Refresh, extend and improve existing analyses and analytical outputs.
Support larger projects by owning clearly defined analytical work packages and producing first analytical drafts.
Develop visualizations or dashboards where they help explain findings or support recurring analysis.
Document analytical logic, assumptions, data limitations and findings clearly.
Work collaboratively with analysts, data scientists, technical teams and business stakeholders.

What you need for this

3–4 years of experience in data analytics, data science or a related role.
Strong SQL and good practical Python skills.
Experience working directly with complex datasets and performing exploratory analysis.
Practical understanding of statistics and analytical methods.
Experience with data visualization and/or dashboarding.
Ability to identify and investigate data-quality or data-availability issues.
Clear analytical documentation and communication skills.
Ability to work effectively within a collaborative team and independently on defined tasks.

Will Be a Plus

Experience with B2C CRM, first-party consumer data or lifecycle/behavioral analytics.
Experience working with offline as well as digital consumer data.
Familiarity with CRM, CDP or marketing automation environments.
Experience analysing data quality, system performance or data flows.
Experience working with proxy signals or incomplete attribution.
Experience with collaborative analytical workflows such as notebooks and Git.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

Hiring And How We Work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Delivery Project Manager (L3).

About The Job

This position is needed to drive the tactical execution and operational delivery of complex cross-functional projects within Global Operations.

As a Delivery Manager, you are the engine of project execution, transforming strategic vision into operational reality. You bridge the gap between business intent and technical execution, ensuring every initiative moves through the lifecycle with precision and speed. By partnering with Enterprise Technology
and being the voice of Global Operations
, you ensure our projects are predictable, transparent, and high-impact, serving as the primary advocate for operational excellence and seamless product rollouts.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

Translate abstract business needs into actionable, prioritized requirements by conducting end-to-end discovery and ensuring both the impact and outcomes of the project are documented.
Cultivate deep partnerships across the Global Operations ecosystem, specifically Global Customer Services, Global Customer Support Operations, and Onboarding & Compliance,to ensure project scalability and total operational readiness.
Drive project momentum by maintaining accountability for timelines and holding cross-functional partners to deadlines while adapting to shifting business capacity.
Identify and mitigate risks by serving as an "early warning system," mapping complex dependencies across Enterprise Technology and Global Operations to protect the critical path.
Generate high-signal, low-noise weekly status updates and maintain rigorous project documentation within Airtable to ensure long-term auditability and stakeholder alignment.
Coordinate launch synchronization between Enterprise Technology releases and Global Operations enablement, ensuring technical deliverables map perfectly to business-facing launch dates.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required:
Experience: 5+ years of experience in Project Management, Program Management, or Delivery Management within a fast-paced technology or operations environment.
Technical Literacy: Proven ability to translate complex technical constraints into business tradeoffs and communicate effectively with Engineering and Product teams.
Execution Skills: Demonstrated expertise in managing end-to-end project lifecycles, including business requirements gathering (BRD), UAT coordination, and launch enablement.
Tooling Proficiency: Advanced experience using project management and tracking tools (e.g., Airtable, Jira, or Asana) to maintain high-integrity documentation.

Desired

Operational Context: Previous experience working closely with Global Operations functions such as Global Customer Services, Global Customer Support Operations, or Onboarding & Compliance.
PMP, or another program management certification

Location

This role will be remote, and based in Colombia.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

Stay alert to recruitment fraud

We care about your safety. Scammers sometimes impersonate Twilio recruiters through fake job postings, emails, websites, or messages. Please ensure you are engaging with an official @twilio.com email address. We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. We do not make job offers without a formal interview process or conduct interviews exclusively through text-based messaging apps.

Twilio is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.
We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers and the California Fair Chance Act. Additionally, Twilio participates in the E-Verify program in certain locations, as required by law.

new_jobs.description:
Department:
R&D

Location:
Remote

Compensation:
$115,000 - $120,000 / year

Description

At Thorne, we work to deliver high-quality, science-backed solutions to empower individuals to take a proactive approach to their well-being. Each day begins with a mission to help others discover and achieve their best health. We count on our team members to challenge and push the boundaries to make that happen. At Thorne, you’ll be joining a team of more than 750 passionate individuals committed to our cause of providing superior health solutions at every age and life stage.

The R&D Tech Ops Project Manager
is responsible for leading complex, cross-functional projects within the Technical Operations segment of Thorne’s Research & Development organization. This role manages multiple workstreams from idea through launch using Thorne’s Stage Gate process, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with established quality and operational requirements.

Projects may include production optimization, quality and compliance initiatives, consumer expectations, cost savings and business continuity, core product growth, technology transfers, and line extensions. The R&D Tech Ops Project Manager establishes project plans, timelines, milestones, risks, and deliverables while creating alignment and accountability across project teams.

Working closely with R&D, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Brand, Finance, Medical, Scientific, Clinical, Regulatory Affairs, and other cross-functional partners, this role serves as a central point of coordination for Technical Operations projects. The ideal candidate combines hands-on manufacturing knowledge with strong project leadership, operational excellence expertise, and the ability to translate complex technical and business requirements into clear, executable project plans.

Travel Requirements:
Approximately 15%

Responsibilities

Lead multiple Technical Operations projects from initial concept through implementation and launch using Thorne’s Stage Gate process and established R&D Project Management Office (PMO) practices.
Serve as the R&D project lead and advocate for assigned Tech Ops initiatives, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, within scope, and at the expected level of quality.
Develop comprehensive project plans, timelines, milestones, deliverables, resource requirements, and success measures for assigned initiatives.
Lead, coordinate, and facilitate cross-functional project teams, establishing clear roles, responsibilities, priorities, and accountability throughout the project lifecycle.
Partner closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Brand, Finance, Medical, Scientific, Clinical, Regulatory Affairs, and other stakeholders to align technical and business requirements.
Manage projects involving production optimization, quality and compliance, cost savings, business continuity, technology transfers, core product growth, consumer expectations, and line extensions.
Proactively identify project risks, dependencies, constraints, and potential roadblocks and develop mitigation and contingency plans to protect project timelines, budgets, scope, and quality.
Monitor project performance against established milestones and proactively address schedule, resource, budget, quality, or execution risks.
Maintain accurate and current project documentation, serving as the central source of truth for project plans, decisions, timelines, deliverables, risks, and status.
Prepare and communicate project status reports, highlighting progress, milestones, risks, challenges, decisions, and recommended solutions for project teams and business stakeholders.
Facilitate project meetings, decision-making discussions, and cross-functional working sessions to drive alignment, accountability, and timely resolution of issues.
Build strong, trusting relationships across project teams and stakeholder groups to promote transparency, collaboration, and effective execution.
Communicate effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization, from production-floor employees and technical subject matter experts to senior executives.
Apply project management and operational excellence methodologies to identify opportunities, improve project execution, and support effective decision-making.
Develop and lead improvement strategies and initiatives that strengthen operational performance and project management effectiveness.
Track project outcomes, lessons learned, successes, and challenges and apply insights to continuously improve future project execution and R&D PMO practices.
Maintain rigor and consistency across project management systems, reporting, documentation, and governance to ensure timely and reliable project information.
Support a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

What You Need

Education & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Science, Engineering, or a related discipline required; Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management, Analytics, or a related field preferred.
5–10 years of professional experience, including at least 3 years of hands-on experience working in a manufacturing or production-floor environment.
At least 2 years of demonstrated experience successfully leading and delivering projects within a manufacturing environment.
Proven experience managing complex, cross-functional projects from initiation through implementation or market launch.
Experience working with Stage Gate processes and project management methodologies supporting new product development, technology transfers, product changes, or line extensions.
Experience working within a regulated manufacturing environment and familiarity with applicable regulatory and quality requirements.
Experience supporting operational excellence, process improvement, manufacturing optimization, or related Technical Operations initiatives.
Project Management certification preferred.
Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, APICS, or related operational excellence certification preferred.

Technical Knowledge

Strong knowledge of project management principles, methodologies, tools, and best practices, including project planning, scheduling, resource management, risk management, and project governance.
Working knowledge of Stage Gate processes and their application to new product development, line extensions, technology transfers, and manufacturing initiatives.
Understanding of manufacturing operations, production workflows, process optimization, and the dependencies between R&D and commercial manufacturing.
Knowledge of operational excellence methodologies, including Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles.
Ability to identify, assess, prioritize, and mitigate project risks while developing practical contingency plans.
Ability to analyze project and operational data and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
Experience with Smartsheet and Power BI for project planning, tracking, reporting, and data visualization.
Familiarity with regulatory compliance and industry-specific standards applicable to regulated manufacturing environments.
Ability to maintain accurate project documentation, reporting, and data to support effective project governance and decision-making.

Core Competencies

Exceptional project leadership skills with the ability to manage multiple complex projects, workstreams, priorities, and cross-functional teams simultaneously.
Strong organizational skills with demonstrated ability to manage timelines, resources, dependencies, and deliverables in a fast-paced environment.
Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills with the ability to establish trust and influence stakeholders across all levels of the organization.
Ability to lead through influence and create accountability across cross-functional teams without relying on direct reporting relationships.
Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable information for technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to communicate effectively with stakeholders ranging from production-floor employees and technical specialists to senior executives.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk-management skills with the ability to identify issues early and develop practical solutions.

Numerous years of experience in managing complex program portfolios, with a proven track record of leading large-scale technology transitions.

new_jobs.title: Staff/Sr Staff Technical Program Manager, Hardware Systems
new_jobs.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

We are hiring a Sr Technical Program Manager (TPM) to drive program execution across Lightmatter's Hardware Systems team. You will drive schedules, resource planning, priorities, and cross-functional alignment for all projects and activities within the team - spanning electrical, mechanical, and system engineering.. You will work closely with internal teams such as SI, PI, SW, supply chain, and with external partners, including contract manufacturers, PCB and sheet metal fabricators, assembly houses, and other suppliers, to keep programs on track from early design through production.

In this role, you will manage dependencies and trade-offs across concurrent workstreams, facilitate alignment across internal and external stakeholders, and maintain program visibility for engineering leadership. Your scope covers the full hardware development lifecycle, from design through production, including the engineering support programs, test infrastructure, and tooling that keep the broader team moving. You will also serve as the team's primary program interface to broader organizational programs, ensuring that schedule changes, material commitments, and engineering status are communicated accurately and on time to cross-functional program stakeholders.

This is a hands-on role that combines strong program management fundamentals with a working knowledge of hardware engineering. You will be equally at home in a design review, a supplier call, a resource planning discussion, and an executive status update. You will also need to thrive in a fast-moving environment where requirements evolve, priorities shift, and not every process is fully established, and bring the clarity and structure that turns that ambiguity into forward progress.

Responsibilities

Own program coordination across all HW Systems activities: maintain an integrated schedule across all concurrent projects and workstreams, surface priority conflicts, and drive resolution of resource contention with engineering leads.
Drive cross-functional alignment between HW Systems and other teams: setting agendas, facilitating meetings, capturing decisions, communicating delays and risks, and relentlessly following up on action items
Manage team-wide resource loading and capacity visibility, partnering with engineering leads to flag overallocation risks and drive trade-offs discussions across concurrent programs
Build and maintain integrated program schedules that reflect hardware development realities - bring-up milestones, NPI phases, EVT/DVT/PVT gates, and cross-team dependencies
Own program scope that lives outside formal project charters: tester boards, demos, lab fixtures, calibration equipment, and internal engineering tools that teams depend on but that would otherwise lack dedicated ownership
Coordinate material flow within the HW Systems team: track component orders, PCB fab runs, PCBA and mechanical assemblies, and engineering samples; partner with supply chain to ensure critical materials land on schedule
Track and coordinate cross-functional teams' HW deliverable dependencies including quantities and timelines, and ensure downstream teams are unblocked with accurate, up-to-date visibility into HW schedule and status
Serve as the primary hardware program interface with external contract manufacturers, PCB and sheet metal fabricators, and assembly houses: managing schedules, tracking deliverables, facilitating technical alignment, and driving closure on open issues in partnership with Supply chain.
Represent the HW Systems team in company-wide program reviews and cross-functional planning cadences; own the team's program interface to broader organizational stakeholders, communicating schedule changes, material needs, and engineering commitments proactively and clearly
Track HW Systems budgets for engineering activities, prototype builds, and tooling; coordinate with finance and operations to ensure spend is planned, visible, and aligned with program milestones
Adapt quickly to change: replan and realign when scope shifts, schedules move, or engineering realities force a pivot; maintain momentum and clarity even when the path forward is not fully defined
Establish and maintain lightweight program management processes: status reporting cadences, risk registers, dependency tracking, and decision logs

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.
5+ years of program management experience in hardware engineering, with direct exposure to electrical and mechanical development cycles.
Proven track record managing concurrent engineering programs with shared resources and overlapping timelines.
Deep familiarity with hardware development processes and terminology across the full lifecycle—including PCBA and mechanical enclosures, PCB fabrication, system integration, bring-up, EVT/DVT/PVT, and production—enabling clear communication with engineers and vendors.
Proven experience coordinating with contract manufacturers (CMs) and ODMs to manage schedules, track deliverables, and resolve open issues.
Hands-on experience with material flow, component tracking, and BOM management.
Skilled facilitator who drives productive meetings, captures critical context, and ensures action items are owned and closed.
Strong written and verbal communicator, comfortable presenting program status and risk assessments to engineering leads and executives.
Expert in project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, Smartsheet, or equivalent platforms.
Strong bias for action—consistently closes loops, follows up independently, and identifies potential slips before they impact project timelines.
Thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments; proactively creates structure and drives clarity without waiting for complete information.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing programs for complex hardware development
Experience defining and improving program management processes in a startup or new business unit

This role is open to two different levels.

Staff: $171,000 - $200,000

Sr Staff: $203,000 - $243,000

We offer competitive compensation. The base salary range for this role determined based on location, experience, educational background, and market data.

Salary Range: total compensation goes beyond base salary, it also includes a new hire equity grant, annual performance-based equity, and other rewards that recognize your impact and contribution.: $171,000 USD - $243,000 USD

Build a Global Outsourcing Strategy from the Ground Up

Dart is seeking a strategic Supplier Outsourcing Program Manager to build and lead our outsourced finished goods program. This is a unique opportunity to create a new capability, bringing structure and strategy to how products are sourced, manufactured, and delivered across our global network.

We're looking for a builder -- someone who has led outsourcing initiatives, developed supplier networks, and driven change across organizations. In this highly visible role, you'll influence sourcing decisions, design global supply chains, and help shape Dart's long-term growth strategy.

If you're energized by creating something new, solving complex business challenges, and making a lasting impact, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do...

Lead development and execution of Dart’s outsourced finished goods strategy for an assigned product portfolio

new_jobs.description:
Description

At 1898 & Co., a division of Burns & McDonnell, our Enterprise Systems Integration (ESI) team partners with clients to modernize and integrate critical Operational Technology (OT) systems across industrial, utility, and infrastructure environments. Our team delivers end‑to‑end solutions supporting resilient operations, secure architectures, complex networks, lifecycle modernization, and the convergence of OT and IT systems.

We are seeking a Project Manager who will lead complex OT‑focused integration projects involving control systems, industrial networking, cybersecurity, and enterprise system connectivity. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership, technical understanding of OT environments, and the ability to coordinate multidisciplinary teams to deliver projects safely, on time, and within budget.

This role requires excellent communication, structured execution, and the ability to guide clients through digital modernization, system upgrades, and large‑scale OT program implementation.

What You’ll Do

Business Development

Identify and pursue new sales opportunities with clients to expand the ESI business line.
Lead proposal development and submission, including project estimation, planning, and scheduling.
Establish critical project objectives and key performance indicators with clients.
Lead contract preparation and negotiation in collaboration with internal teams and clients.
Develop and maintain long-term relationships with client stakeholders, acting as a trusted partner in their data and analytics journey.

Project Execution

Lead program estimation, planning, and budgeting activities, maintaining accountability for project execution and delivery.
Adopt, implement, and adjust leading project delivery methodologies, including both Waterfall and Agile approaches.
Manage full project lifecycles, ensuring alignment with client goals and adherence to schedule, budget, and quality expectations.
Track and report overall project status, milestones, deliverables, and financial performance metrics.
Create and deliver detailed project status reports and lead regular stakeholder meetings covering schedule, risks, issues, budget, and resource allocation.
Supervise and coordinate all project resources, including internal 1898 & Co. teams, client personnel, and third-party vendors.
Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards and contractual obligations.
Support and oversee project deliverables assigned to both onshore and offshore teams, ensuring alignment with project objectives.
Conduct quality assurance reviews of all deliverables to verify compliance with standards and best practices.
Ensure adherence to company safety policies and quality standards throughout all project activities.
Serve as the central point of contact for project interdependencies, ensuring seamless coordination between internal and external stakeholders.
Utilize project management experience to influence project execution processes and quality assurance/quality control protocols.

Leadership & Mentorship

Provide leadership and direction to multidisciplinary project teams, fostering collaboration and accountability.
Mentor and develop team members by sharing knowledge and best practices related to project management, analytics, and digital transformation.
Promote a culture of teamwork, customer commitment, and continuous improvement within the ESI group.
Champion innovation in project delivery and encourage adoption of new tools and methodologies that enhance client outcomes.
Support staff development through coaching and professional growth opportunities.

Technical Responsibilities

Lead and oversee the business process design phase to capture system requirements, including functional, technical, integration, and security needs.
Validate that system requirements align with business processes, project scope, and strategic goals.
Collaborate with staff managers to identify and develop training and performance support materials for project rollouts.
Lead requirements gathering and business process design for OT systems including control systems, SCADA, historians, OT networks, edge devices, asset management platforms, and enterprise‑connected systems.
Ensure requirements cover functional, technical, cybersecurity, integration, network, and reliability needs.
Validate alignment between system requirements, business processes, operational constraints, and enterprise integration goals.
Coordinate development of training, documentation, and change‑management materials supporting OT system rollouts.
Provide guidance on digital modernization involving control system upgrades, data acquisition strategies, telecom architectures, and secure network segmentation.
Ensure alignment with cybersecurity best practices and governance standards across all OT system work.

Preferred Experience And Skills

Understanding of complex OT systems and telecommunications used by power utilities
Understanding of technologies such as ADMS, DERMS, DCS, OMS, EMS, SCADA
Understanding of electric system operations for Distribution or Generation

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, Computer Science, Information Technology or related degree from accredited program.
Minimum 5 years of experience providing Project or Program Management with at least 2 years focused on operational technology projects or programs including the ability to demonstrate having worked on multiple large projects or programs.
Previous large project or program leadership experience is preferable.
Must demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills, strong interpersonal skills, and the ability to clearly and effectively present complex information to all levels of employees, management, and clients.
Experience with electric utility clients implementing and integrating operational systems such as OMS, DMS, ADMS, AMI, DERMS, IEC-61850, SCADA, Telecom FAN is preferred.
Professional certifications related to Program or Project management such as PMP or Agile SAFe are a plus.
Experience with a variety of project execution methodologies including but not limited to Waterfall and Agile.
Position requires the ability to thoughtfully and positively influence, lead, and manage change.
Must possess strong leadership skills, interpersonal skills, project management experience, and a strategic perspective.
Must be proficient in the use of computer software (i.e., Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Travel 30% of the time.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Vacuum Process Engineering, Inc.
, known as VPE, is an exciting special-process manufacturing company for defense, semiconductor, energy markets that is growing. VPE technologies have applications in defense, medical, semiconductor, energy, and commercial aviation. There is never a dull day at VPE; we’ve been in business for 45 years and have 5 buildings with over 200,000 sq. ft. of manufacturing space. We offer competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package. We are seeking an additional team member for our process engineering and innovation staff; a dedicated individual with good work ethics that is seeking a long-term career with a stable company.

Pay Range: 150-175k, depending on experience

Please note that if you do not meet the required experience for this position, you will not be considered for this opening.

Objective:

We are seeking a high-performance Program Manager to play a foundational role in building and scaling a newly received, strategically significant program at VPE. This customer represents a high-growth opportunity with clear trajectory toward large-volume production, and this individual will be instrumental in establishing the program infrastructure, processes, and team needed to meet that demand. The right candidate brings proven experience scaling customers from prototype through automation and high-volume manufacturing — understanding how to architect the transition from early-stage development to repeatable, efficient production at scale. This individual will own the full program lifecycle — from initial customer engagement and proposal development through production execution, delivery, and ongoing account growth — serving as the single point of contact for all program communications. The ideal candidate combines the disciplined rigor of an engineer with the commercial acumen of a business developer and the motivational presence of a natural leader.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Serve as the exclusive single point of contact for the assigned customer account, owning all program communications from kickoff through delivery and post-delivery support.
Establish and maintain executive-level customer relationships, driving satisfaction, retention, and organic revenue growth.
Prepare and present program status reports, risk registers, and corrective action plans to senior leadership and customer stakeholders.
Proactively identify risks, issues, and opportunities within each program and deploy mitigation strategies before escalation is required.
Own and manage the full program portfolio from NPI (New Product Introduction) through production ramp and steady-state delivery.
Develop and maintain a customer growth roadmap, tracking opportunities from identification through award.
Deliver accurate monthly program financial forecasts and variance analyses to finance and executive leadership.
Manage program-level P&L including revenue recognition, cost-to-complete forecasting, gross margin analysis, and working capital optimization.
Lead quality planning processes including the development of inspection and test plans (ITPs), first article inspections (FAIs), non-conformance resolution, and customer witness point coordination.
Drive procurement strategy and execution in partnership with supply chain; manage critical path items, long-lead components, and supplier performance.
Drive a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across all program touchpoints.
Resolve cross-functional conflicts through structured facilitation and consensus-building techniques.

Required Qualifications:

B.S. or M.S. in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Petroleum, or related field).
10+ years of PM experience in contract manufacturing, aerospace, or green energy sectors.
Proven track record of scaling a customer program from prototype and pilot production through process automation and high-volume manufacturing; this is a foundational requirement given VPE’s mandate to grow this newly received program to full-rate production.
Demonstrated success managing programs with P&L responsibility of $5M or greater.
Strong working knowledge of contract manufacturing processes: fabrication, machining, assembly, integration, and test.
Proficiency with ERP platforms, MS Project or equivalent scheduling tools, and advanced Excel/data analytics.
Track record of leading and growing customer accounts in a competitive, multi-vendor environment.
Experience with quality management systems and regulatory/industry standards applicable to energy and industrial markets.

Preferred Qualifications:

PMP or PMP certification through PMI.
APICS CPIM or CSCP supply chain certification.
Exposure to FEED (Front-End Engineering Design) to EPC project execution models.
Experience with IOGP, API, ATEX, or similar energy sector standards.
Background in solar, wind, energy storage, hydrogen, or other renewable energy manufacturing programs.

new_jobs.title: Program Security Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Metrea delivers effects-as-a-service to national security partners across five domains and more than a dozen mission areas. These include airborne ISR, electronic warfare, secure communications, aerial refuelling, special air missions, aerial firefighting, and advanced simulation. We own the whole stack: designing, building, and operating turnkey capabilities that give our partners decisive, asymmetric advantage against rapidly evolving threats.

Our operating model is built around three interlocking pillars. The Support Groups provide a global shared-service – spanning people, finance, platform, operations, legal, and engagement. This frees up our Core Groups, who develop and own mission capabilities end-to-end, to focus entirely on delivery. The Market Groups apply a regional lens, ensuring that our agile and adaptable capabilities remain aligned to the wicked problems that matter most to our partners across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

At the heart of our model is a simple but powerful idea: be a true partner with skin in the game. Our partners need effects, not just equipment. By owning the full stack – from the lab to the field – we are able to drive a continuous cycle of innovation that keeps our partners ahead. It's a fast-moving, intellectually demanding environment where talented people are given real responsibility, work on problems that matter, and contribute to an enterprise that is growing quickly and deliberately.

Headquartered in Washington, DC, with facilities across the United States, the United Kingdom, as well as Continental Europe and Asia-Pacific.

Group Overview

Electromagnetic and Cyber Group (EM&C) is responsible for developing flexible and survivable advanced electronic warfare and secure communications equipment while providing the industry’s leading signals intelligence, electronic warfare, and cyber experts.  Metrea specializes in signal classification, direction finding, advanced geolocation techniques, and waveform development including waveforms for MANET and LPI/LPD applications. Metrea also develops special purpose radios for government customers and licenses DF and geolocation solutions to multiple OEMs. 

Position Summary

The Program Security Manager is responsible for developing, coordinating, and sustaining the security, risk mitigation, and mission assurance framework required to support sensitive operational programs. This role integrates counter-intelligence awareness, operational security, collection management support, and planning discipline to help protect personnel, capabilities, partners, infrastructure, and activities across complex mission environments.

This position supports programs that may involve distributed teams, compartmented information, operational ambiguity, non-standard infrastructure, sensitive partnerships, and time-sensitive requirements. The Program Security Manager works across program leadership, operations personnel, planners, technical teams, vendors, and government stakeholders to identify risk, strengthen controls, support decision-making, and ensure practical security oversight is built into planning and execution.

What You'll Do

Serve as the primary security, risk, and mission assurance advisor for sensitive programs and operational activities.
Assess threats, vulnerabilities, and operational risks related to personnel, partners, facilities, technology, supply chains, access, infrastructure, and the information environment.
Support planning and execution of sensitive activities by integrating counter-intelligence, operational security, risk mitigation, and collection management considerations.
Develop and maintain risk assessments, mitigation plans, decision briefs, operational security products, and executive-level recommendations.
Review operational concepts, plans, activities, and proposed partnerships to identify security risks, exposure concerns, compliance issues, or potential adversary exploitation paths.
Coordinate with program managers, operators, planners, technical personnel, vendors, partners, and government stakeholders to ensure risk mitigation measures are practical, executable, and aligned with mission requirements.
Support collection management and reporting workflows, including requirements tracking, reporting review, information management, and feedback on operational relevance.
Help identify intelligence gaps, information requirements, and collection priorities that support operational planning, threat understanding, and decision-making.
Contribute to operational planning products such as CONOPS, briefings, decision papers, risk matrices, after-action reviews, and mitigation recommendations.
Monitor ongoing activities to ensure security controls, OPSEC practices, and mitigation measures remain effective as the mission environment changes.
Support incident reviews, anomaly assessments, and lessons-learned processes to identify root causes, potential compromise, and corrective actions.
Prepare and deliver clear, concise briefings to senior leaders and stakeholders on operational risk, threat posture, mitigation options, and mission impact.
Help build repeatable processes for sensitive program security, documentation, oversight, deconfliction, and risk governance.

What You Bring

20+ years of combined experience in SOF, Intelligence Community, Department of Defense, interagency, or sensitive commercial operations.
Strong understanding of counter-intelligence, operational security, risk mitigation, and sensitive activity support.
Experience evaluating risk to personnel, infrastructure, technology, access, vendors, partners, supply chains, or operational plans.
Ability to translate complex threat, security, and intelligence information into practical recommendations for operators and senior leaders.
Familiarity with intelligence cycle activities, collection requirements, operational reporting, information management, and decision-support products.
Experience supporting operational planning, mission management, staff coordination, or effects-based planning.
Ability to work independently in ambiguous, fast-moving, and sensitive environments with limited oversight.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare executive-level briefings, assessments, and formal recommendations.
Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to protect sensitive information while enabling operational outcomes.
Experience developing or reviewing CONOPS, OPORDs, operational briefs, risk assessments, information papers, or senior-leader decision products.
Familiarity with FIE threat analysis, pattern-of-life analysis, vulnerability assessment, operational deconfliction, or adversary targeting methodologies.
Experience coordinating with government customers, operational units, partner organizations, vendors, or interagency stakeholders.
Understanding of Intelligence Community policies, oversight requirements, reporting standards, or collection management processes.
Must be a U.S. citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.

Additional Eligibility Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of relevant experience; additional operational, military, intelligence, or government experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
Completion of a recognized U.S. Government or DoD source-handling certification course, such as Category I HUMINT or equivalent.
Demonstrated experience supporting sensitive operations, intelligence activities, national security programs, or risk-managed operational environments.
Experience producing written assessments, briefings, reports, mitigation plans, or decision-support products.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, operate with discretion, and support time-sensitive requirements.
Active TS/SCI clearance preferred.

HSA/FSA accounts

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

Role Overview

Some of the world's largest companies and their law firms use Harvey’s AI capabilities to deliver world-class client services at unprecedented scale and efficiency. Harvey allows high-performing professionals to gain deep domain knowledge faster, understand the big picture, and tackle more complex challenges in less time.

Our customers depend on us to deliver a secure, trustworthy, and compliant platform. Earning the trust of our customers is a business enabler and we value it more than anything else.

In this role, you will report to the Head of Trust and serve as the primary leader for the Customer Trust function. You will build and lead a high-performing team across time zones (US, UK, and beyond) to address customer security inquiries, support our Go-To-Market (GTM) team with accurate and timely responses, and elevate our overall security posture. You will operate at the intersection of technical security, customer success, audit, and AI innovation, leveraging Harvey’s own tools to improve the speed, automation, and accuracy of our responses. This is a unique opportunity to shape the customer trust narrative, manage our Trust Center, and empower Harvey to win complex deals.

Customer & AE Partnership: Act as the primary technical point of contact for our Go-To-Market (GTM) team and customers regarding security questions. Provide timely, accurate, and empathetic responses to questionnaires and concerns, ensuring we answer customer questions and unblock deals while maintaining high security standards.
AI-Powered Automation: Leverage AI and Harvey’s internal tools to continuously improve the efficiency and accuracy of our response process. Build scalable workflows to reduce manual overhead and improve response times while optimizing quality.
Metrics & Reporting: Establish and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) for the Customer Trust function. Use data to track team impact, response velocity, quality of answers, and the influence of trust on sales outcomes.

Job Description:

Apply your expertise to advance the mission and optimize our business strategy as a Site Security Manager (SSM)
II at GDIT.

As a Site Security Manager (SSM) II you are responsible for the security aspects of project planning, design and construction. The SSM is also responsible to ensure compliance of all regulatory requirements for the accreditation of the facility. Planners, Project Managers, Design Managers, Designers, and Construction Managers must work closely with the supported command and their designated SSM to determine the requirements for each project and ensure the implementation of the policy-based requirements.

Responsibilities:

Develops and implements a Concept Validation Request (CVR), Construction Security Plan (CSP), Pre-Con/Fixed Facility Checklist (FFC), construction oversight Standard Operating Procedures, and all TEMPEST documentation.
Conducts periodic security inspections for the duration of the project to ensure compliance with the CSP and Accrediting Official (AO) requirements.
Documents security violations or deviations of the CSP and notifies the AO within required timeframes.
Works with the construction firm(s) to ensure security of the construction site, construction materials, equipment, site access and compliance with the requirements set forth in the CSP.
Works with applicable AO to mitigate construction and physical strategies to counter security and counterintelligence threats.
Ensure strict adherence to the provisions of the NISPOM, its Supplement, the DoD Overprint, DCID, ICD, applicable UFCs, and SAP policies.
Provide day-to-day SSM associated security staff oversight including continuous assessment of procedures to identify shortfalls and provide appropriate recommendations for revising and improving security policies, procedures, and systems.
Ensures timely notification of pertinent security matters to program technical and management staff.
Ensures the construction project meets the requirements of the ICD 705 Tech Spec, UFC 4-010-05 and the requirements of the customer.
Shall attend all project planning meetings, design reviews, and contractor specific progress/planning meetings providing security input, ensuring customer requirements will comply with the ICD 705 Tech Spec.
Ensures photo documentation is completed for the life cycle of the construction project and retained in accordance with regulations.
Shall evaluate each proposed Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) & Special Access Program Facility spaces for threats, vulnerabilities, and assets to determine the most efficient countermeasures required for physical and technical security.
Brief all levels of personnel, both in the government and senior civilian services, on a variety of security related topics.
Must be proficient in professional briefings, technical writing, and correspondence.
Ensure policy requirements are implemented; advise AO of compliance and variances.
Provide leadership, performance mentoring, and administrative oversight of team members
Deliver to the accrediting official Intrusion Detection Reports, Sound Transmission Class (STC) Reports, Radio Frequency (RF) Testing Reports.
Develop all required accreditation documentation to include completed FFC, TEMPEST Checklist, Compartmented Area Checklist (if required), Co-Utilization Agreements, Accreditation Memorandums, Controlled Area Designation Letter (if required), Common Operating Authorization Letters (if required), SOPs, and Emergency Action Plans.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Education

Bachelor’s degree is desired and counts towards 4 years of experience. Associates degree counts towards 2 years of experience.

Experience

3+ years related experience
SAP experience required
Experience with physical security, personnel management and/or construction management

Education And Experience Equivalents:

1 year of experience for each SPeD certification
Maximum equivalent experience for SPeD certifications/credentials will be no more than 3 years.
Certification/credential examples:
Security Fundamentals Professional Certification (SFPC)
Security Asset Protection Professional Certification (SAPPC)
Special Program Security Credential (SPSC)
Security Program Integration Professional Certification (SPIPC)
Physical Security Certification (PSC)
Industrial Security Oversight Credential (ISOC)
Antiterrorism Credential (ATC)

Security Clearance

Required: TS/SCI
Must be willing to obtain CI polygraph

Other Requirements

Complete additional safety training and/or certification as required by local site (i.e. OSHA 30 Construction Safety, OSHA Fall Protection and OSHA Confined Space) within the first 90 days of hire
Must obtain CDSE STEPP ICD 705 Physical Security Construction Requirements for SAP course completion within the first 30 days of hire
Must be able to pass a Site Security Manager Certification course within first 12 months
Must be able to lift up to 40lbs to examine product deliveries.
Must be able to walk long distances and up and down stairs.

new_jobs.title: Physical Security Manager (GSOC)
new_jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence . As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

We're seeking an experienced Manager, Global Security Operations Center (GSOC) to lead the day-to-day operations of Crusoe's Global Security Operations Center; the 24/7/365 command center responsible for monitoring, intelligence, incident response, and operational coordination that protects our people, facilities, and critical infrastructure worldwide.

Reporting to the Director, Global Physical Security, you'll lead the operational execution of the GSOC while helping scale its people, processes, and capabilities to support Crusoe's rapid global growth all while protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability across all lines of business. You'll translate strategic priorities into operational excellence by building a high-performing team, driving continuous improvement, and ensuring the GSOC delivers exceptional service across an increasingly diverse portfolio of corporate offices, manufacturing facilities, data centers, power generation sites, and construction projects.

This role is ideal for an operational leader who enjoys building programs in a fast-moving environment where every day presents new opportunities to improve, innovate, and mature security operations. You'll play a key role in developing the next generation of Crusoe's GSOC while partnering across the business to deliver a unified, intelligence-driven, always-on security capability.

What You'll Be Working On:

Lead Global GSOC Operations

Lead the day-to-day operation of Crusoe's 24/7/365 Global Security Operations Center, ensuring consistent, high-quality monitoring, incident response, alarm management, and situational awareness across the global enterprise.
Maintain operational readiness across all shifts while ensuring standardized execution of SOPs, escalation procedures, and service-level expectations.
Serve as the operational leader for the GSOC, exercising sound judgment and decisive leadership during critical incidents while maintaining exceptional customer service under pressure.

Incident & Crisis Management

Lead operational response during security incidents, emergencies, and crises by assessing threats, coordinating cross-functional response efforts, dispatching security personnel or emergency responders, initiating mass notification when appropriate, and providing timely, accurate updates to leadership.
Conduct after-action reviews following significant incidents and drive continuous improvement through documented and socialized lessons learned and corrective actions for audit evidence repository.

Business Continuity and Resiliency

Maintain continuity of monitoring and incident response through redundant systems, failover procedures, and a defined backup/alternate-site capability so GSOC operations survive loss of primary facility, network, or power.
Own GSOC-specific business continuity and disaster recovery plans, validated through regular failover testing and tabletop exercises.
Ensure resiliency of the underlying security infrastructure at monitored sites: power, network, and system redundancy for access control, video, and alarm platforms, in partnership with data center and infrastructure teams.

Intelligence & Situational Awareness

Oversee enterprise-wide situational awareness through monitoring of physical security systems, open-source intelligence, commercial threat databases, social media, weather events, geopolitical developments, and other relevant intelligence sources.
Lead the production and quality of GSOC intelligence products, including threat assessments, intelligence briefs, BOLOs, travel advisories, executive support products, and incident reports that enable informed business decisions.
Ensure intelligence products are timely, actionable, and aligned with business priorities.
Protection of sensitive GSOC information: intelligence products, surveillance footage, access records, investigative case files, and executive travel/protection details, with appropriate handling, classification, and need-to-know access controls.

Technology Operations & Continuous Improvement

Lead the operational use and continuous improvement of Crusoe's integrated security technology ecosystem, including enterprise access control, biometric authentication, video management, AI-enabled video analytics, incident management, protective intelligence, mass notification, and monitoring platforms.
Identify opportunities to improve operator workflows, preserve system(s) audit integrity (log completeness, system timestamp accuracy, tamper-evident records and investigative chain-of-custody records) automation, response times, system utilization, and service quality through technology optimization and operational enhancements.
Partner with internal stakeholders and technology owners to support new capabilities, integrations, testing, and operational adoption.

Team Leadership & Vendor Management

Build, lead, and develop a high-performing GSOC organization through coaching, mentoring, training, career development, succession planning, and performance management across all shifts.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, and continuous learning.
Own the operational management of GSOC staffing partners, including recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, scheduling, coaching, quality assurance, performance management, and vendor accountability against established SLAs.
Ensure staffing levels, shift coverage, and operational readiness meet business requirements as Crusoe continues to grow.

Program Growth & Operational Excellence

Develop scalable operating models, onboarding playbooks, and standardized procedures that enable new facilities, regions, and business units to be efficiently integrated into GSOC operations.
Drive operational maturity through process improvement initiatives, tabletop exercises, audits, training programs, and recurring program reviews.
Own and be accountable for the GSOC's operational KPIs end to end — spanning detection and response performance, security system and device health and availability, alarm and intelligence quality, SOP compliance, GSOC evidence completeness, access log retention health, operator training, and investigative case management and hold the team and staffing vendors to defined targets through dashboards, recurring reviews, and executive reporting.
Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, reduce operational risk, and elevate the overall maturity of the GSOC.

Compliance and Audit Support

Ensure GSOC operations, logging, and records satisfy the physical-security control requirements of Crusoe’s compliance frameworks (ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2), including access monitoring, alarm response, visitor management, and incident documentation.
Maintain audit-ready evidence: access logs, alarm and event records, response timelines, and SOP adherence, with defined retention aligned to control and customer contract requirements.

Executive & Employee Support

Establish and maintain a white-glove service culture for every interaction with employees, executives, visitors, and business partners.
Provide operational support for executive travel, special events, high-profile meetings, and other sensitive business activities requiring enhanced security coordination.
Maintain leadership presence through participation in an on-call rotation and provide leadership support during nights, weekends, and holidays when operational needs require.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

5+ years in GSOC/Corporate Security Operations, including 2–3+ years leading shift-based teams and/or managing contract security vendors.
Proven experience leading 24/7 multi-shift operations and managing shift-based and/or contracted teams.
Demonstrated experience managing contracted security personnel and vendor selection, performance management, scheduling, and SLAs.
Strong working knowledge of modern GSOC technology and tools: access control, video and AI-driven video analytics, investigative and open-source databases, mass notification, and incident-management and protective-intelligence platforms; with the ability to operate and optimize such systems rather than select them.
Working familiarity with physical-security controls under common compliance frameworks (ISO27001, SOCII Type 2, or similar / more restrictive).
Experience scaling operations to support organizational growth (new sites, regions, or service expansion).
Sound judgment and decisiveness under pressure; data-driven approach to decisions, metrics, and KPI ownership.
Executive-ready written and verbal communication; foundational knowledge of computer networking and telecommunications; advanced MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)

Bonus Points

ASIS certification (CPP, PSP), Certified Security Operations Center Analyst (CSOCA); Lean Six Sigma; PMP.
Comprehensive understanding of GSOC policies, procedures, and industry best practices.
Background in intelligence analysis, emergency management, business continuity, or risk intelligence.c
Experience supporting a global, multi-site footprint, industrial, aerospace, manufacturing, or other data center, power generation sites and/or critical-infrastructure environments is a plus as well as time zone distributed operations.
Familiarity with travel-risk / duty-of-care programs.
Bachelor's degree, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Operating Conditions

24/7 Global Security Operations Center supporting global business operations.
Rotating schedule across shifts (day, evening, overnight, weekends, holidays) to ensure leadership coverage and support critical incidents; on-call availability for escalations.
Occasional travel in support of growth projects and global security initiatives.

What Success Looks Like

Smooth, consistent day-to-day operations across all shifts, with strong SLA and KPI performance.
A capable, accountable team and a strong staffing-vendor partnership, with the right personnel in place.
The confidence of leadership, stakeholders, and partners in the GSOC's reliability and judgment, and a consistently white-glove experience for employees and executives.
A clear, actionable plan to scale GSOC coverage ahead of upcoming growth projects.

Benefits:

Job Description

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

Insitu, a subsidiary of Boeing, has pioneered the design, manufacturing and operation of high-performance Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) with superior payload capabilities. Insitu’s world-class manufacturing facilities are located in Bingen, WA and deliver the highest quality products on time. We are on a mission to be the world’s most trusted partner; developing and integrating world-class solutions that support customer success in the most challenging environments. Discover a career in Aviation where you are a part of the UAS future while working in a supportive environment focused on Pioneering, Performing, Caring and Unity.

Join our dynamic Security team and help protect our organization from evolving threats. We are seeking a Threat Intelligence Analyst with expertise in investigative analysis, threat intelligence, digital forensic, security monitoring, and risk mitigation. Your work will directly support our Insider Threat Program, cybersecurity program, and broader information security initiatives, helping safeguard critical assets and ensure compliance with security best practices. Help protect classified information systems and sensitive organizational data from internal and external threats.

Key Responsibilities:

Use intelligence aggregation tools to review and assess potential insider threats.
Monitor for concerning behaviors and escalate high-risk incidents for investigation.
Conduct investigative activities including forensic acquisition and analysis of digital assets, interview planning, gathering statements, and resolving allegations.
Recover stolen intellectual property and perform forensic analysis of systems or malware as required.
Produce clear, detailed reports documenting investigative findings, outcomes, and security incidents.
Partner with Security, HR, Legal, and other stakeholders to coordinate investigations and remedial actions
Develop and refine investigation metrics, dashboards, case studies, and trend analyses to support program improvement and decision-making
Plan, implement, upgrade, and monitor computer network/information security measures and controls.
Serve as ISSO/ISSM for multiple classified information systems, ensuring compliance with applicable government and organizational cyber security requirements.
Identify security needs and develop system security plans; coordinate implementation of security architecture and applications.
Oversee security sustainment activities including account management, media protection, audit logging, and secure file processes
Perform risk assessments, penetration testing, system log analysis, and vulnerability evaluations.
Develop and execute risk remediation plans, recommend security technologies.
Conduct user compliance monitoring and address organizational security deficiencies.
Develop, deliver, and update security awareness training and materials.
Assist with maintaining ongoing security infrastructure, update cyber protection measures, and research or develop incident response tools and processes.
Produce intelligence products (alerts, briefs, reports) that translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable guidance for stakeholders.
Perform proactive threat hunting in classified and unclassified environments to identify anomalous behavior and previously undetected threats.

Education & Experience:

Technical bachelor’s degree and 5 or more years related work experience or a master’s degree with 3 or more years or equivalent work experience.
Proven experience in threat intelligence, insider threat analysis, cyber security, and information security investigations.
Strong analytical skills; ability to review and assess intelligence and monitor indicators of compromise.
Experience with intelligence aggregation tools, vulnerability assessment, and risk remediation.
Proficiency in forensic analysis, log analysis, penetration testing, and malware investigation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of producing clear investigative and security reports.
Knowledge of security architecture, firewalls, and safeguarding procedures.
Familiarity with incident response and recovery steps for security breaches.
Meticulous attention to detail and strong problem-solving skills, ensuring thorough analysis and effective threat response.
Demonstrated ability to exercise discretion, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive information appropriately.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance
Familiarity with scripting or automation (e.g. python, powershell)
Knowledge of RMF and government cybersecurity guidance (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CNSSI 1253), and related authorization frameworks.
Experience or familiarity with common information security tools, such as: EDR, Firewall, SIEM, Email Archiver, SEG, DSP, Forensic Suites, eDiscovery, UBA, MDM, and HW/SW write blockers

Preferred Education and Experience:

Degree in Information Security, Cyber Security, Computer Science, Criminal Justice or related field preferred.
Professional cybersecurity or forensic certification desired (e.g. A+, Security+, CISSP, GCIA, GCFA, GCFE, CFCE, ENCE, or similar)

page
to learn more about our benefits, 9/80 work schedule and flexible work model.

We let the type of work you do determine the collaboration style. That means we're not always working in an office, but we continue to gather for key moments of collaboration and connection.

This role will need to be in the office for in-person collaboration at minimum once per quarter and therefore needs to be within commutable distance from Bingen, WA.

Why work at AdvanSix?

Total Rewards program includes a competitive compensation, health, dental, vision & wellness programs, paid vacation, 401K with company matching, health savings programs, disability & life insurance, employee assistance program

Work within a fast paced and innovative company, meeting passionate colleagues and partners with diverse backgrounds and experiences

The Health, Safety & Security Manager
is responsible for ensuring the facility operates in a safe and secure manner and in compliance with all company, local, state, and federal regulatory requirements. This role champions Health & Safety excellence across the site by leading programs, processes, and initiatives that drive a strong safety culture, regulatory compliance, risk reduction, and continuous improvement.

The Health & Safety Manager serves as a trusted advisor to site leadership and provides technical safety expertise across all levels of the organization. This is a working leader position with direct reports and reports to the Plant Manager. The role is responsible for leading the site's Health & Safety programs and continuous improvement initiatives.

Essential Responsibilities

Develop and implement tools, programs, and initiatives that increase safety awareness, engagement, accountability, and capability across the site.
Lead by example and actively coach, mentor, and influence employees and contractors to strengthen the site's safety culture and commitment to safe work practices.
Ensure site security programs and related compliance requirements are maintained in accordance with company standards.
Lead and develop Safety team and other assigned personnel through coaching, performance management, and professional development.
Monitor, analyze, and communicate Health & Safety performance metrics to identify trends, drive continuous improvement, and achieve site objectives.
Partner with site leadership to establish safety goals, priorities, and strategies that support business objectives and operational excellence.
Ensure compliance with company policies, standards, and applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including OSHA requirements.
Support the development, delivery, and continuous improvement of safety training programs for employees and contractors.
Provide technical safety expertise and consultation for facility projects, process changes, equipment installations, and operational improvements.
Coordinate site health and safety assessments, including industrial hygiene monitoring, ergonomic evaluations, insurance reviews, and internal audits.
Lead incident investigations and root cause analyses, ensuring corrective actions are identified, implemented, verified, and sustained.
Ensure OSHA recordable, lost-time, and other required safety metrics are accurately reported and maintained.
Lead Safety Committee activities and actively participate as a member of the site leadership team.
Support the site's Responsible Care® 14001 / ISO management systems, including audits, corrective actions, management reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Support compliance assurance activities and internal auditing processes to verify adherence to company standards and regulatory requirements.
Support management of change, including risk assessments, safety reviews, and implementation of new initiatives. Share best practices across the organization and actively contribute to corporate safety initiatives.
Ensure contractor safety programs are effectively implemented and that contractor work activities meet site safety expectations and requirements.
Develop, maintain, and periodically test the site's Emergency Response Plan and Business Continuity Plan.
Maintain required records and documentation in accordance with company and regulatory retention requirements.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Environmental Health & Safety, or a related discipline; or equivalent combination of education and significant relevant experience.
Minimum 7+ years of progressive Health & Safety experience in a manufacturing, chemical, petrochemical, utility, pharmaceutical, energy, or heavy industrial environment.
Minimum 3 years of leadership, supervisory, or people-management experience.
Demonstrated knowledge of OSHA regulations and occupational safety management systems.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in chemical manufacturing, petrochemical, energy, or other highly regulated industrial environments.
Experience working in a Process Safety Management site
Prior experience working in a MARSEC or similarly highly regulated environment
Demonstrated success leading safety culture transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
Experience conducting incident investigations, root cause analyses, and corrective action management.
Experience supporting Responsible Care® 14001, RC14001, ISO management systems, or similar compliance frameworks.
Strong communication, presentation, facilitation, and influencing skills.
Strong technical writing skills, including policies, procedures, standards, and training materials.
Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), or other relevant professional certification preferred.
